title: Belleville, Ont., police to give update on motive behind shooting near synagogue

image.caption: Belleville police are still outside the Sons of Jacob Synagogue on Thursday. (Michelle Song/CBC)

blocks.text: Belleville, Ont., police to provide update on shootout near synagogue
Police in Belleville, Ont., are set to speak to media at 2 p.m. Thursday to provide an update on the ongoing investigation into Sunday night's shooting outside the Sons of Jacob Synagogue.

items: Belleville’s police chief is expected to tell reporters about what motivated Sunday’s shooting near the Sons of Jacob Synagogue at 2 p.m. ET.
Ontario’s solicitor general, who oversees public safety in the province, is also expected in Belleville.
Police have not spoken specifically about what brought the shooter Sean Ward to the area with a shotgun. Ward was fatally injured that night.
Const. Jeff Smith of Belleville police was badly injured and faces a “long, difficult road” ahead, according to his wife.

September 24Muslim organization showing upBelleville police are still outside the Sons of Jacob Synagogue on Thursday. (Michelle Song/CBC)Hi, I’m Michelle Song. I’m in Belleville today for the news conference.We headed to the Sons of Jacob Synagogue first, where we saw Ontario Solicitor General Michael Kerzner speaking with police outside. Mohammed Beebeejaun with the Islamic Society of Belleville was also exiting the synagogue this afternoon after dropping off flowers and a card. Beebeejaun says Belleville is a tight-knit community and it was important for the Islamic society to show support for the Jewish community. “We sympathize with them. And we told them we are here to help them with whatever they need,” he said.

Ontario's Jewish community reacts with horror to the violenceGuy QuennevilleCommunity holds vigil in downtown Belleville following shootingCommunity members, elected officials and religious leaders gathered outside city hall in Belleville, Ont., for a vigil on Monday, after a suspect allegedly opened fire on a police officer near a local synagogue.While Belleville police have not yet divulged any findings about what led Ward to that area Sunday night, one of the synagogue's windows was left with multiple bullet holes. Leaders of Ontario's Jewish community have roundly condemned Sunday's incident as a targeted hate crime. Ontario's police watchdog, which is also investigating Belleville police, has said that Ward got to within half a block of the synagogue. Asked Monday whether the evidence suggested it was an attack aimed specifically at the Jewish community, a spokesperson for the watchdog replied: "I'd be speculating, but ... I think that common sense would say that probably was the case."

Smith faces a 'long, difficult' road to recoveryGuy QuennevilleBelleville police Const. Jeff Smith in a photo shared by his wife Ashley. (Ashley Smith/Facebook)Smith has been with the Belleville police since 2013. He was parked near the synagogue because the congregation had requested police protection — a routine practice going back years, according to the president of the synagogue. Smith's wife, Ashley Smith, wrote in a Facebook post Tuesday night that Smith was unable to speak for himself and required treatment by a neurosurgeon. She offered no other specifics about her husband's medical condition but wrote, "Jeff has a very long, difficult road ahead."

What we know about the Sunday shootingGuy QuennevilleBelleville police and Ontario's Special Investigations Unit at the scene on Monday. (Ian MacAlpine/The Canadian Press)Belleville police Const. Jeff Smith was stationed outside the Sons of Jacob Synagogue, located in a residential area of the city, when 29-year-old Sean Ward fired at him with a shotgun. Smith returned fire. Another Belleville officer also fired their weapon. Smith was critically injured, while Ward suffered life-threatening injuries and later died in hospital.

Belleville police to give update at 2 p.m. ETGuy QuennevilleFour days after a Belleville police officer was critically wounded near a local synagogue holding a Yom Kippur service, the police force is hosting a news conference Thursday at 2 p.m. ET. Belleville police Chief Murray Rodd will be on hand to give remarks, joined by Ontario Solicitor General Michael Kerzner.
